items.title: Google launches connected AI tools including Gemini study notebooks and no-cost practice ACT and GRE tests to personalize student learning and test preparation [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Supporting students with connected AI tools for more personalized learning
items.summary:
Google has introduced new connected AI tools aimed at enhancing personalized learning and test preparation for students. These include Gemini study notebooks, which create adaptive, interactive lessons tailored to individual learning goals, and no-cost practice tests for the ACT and GRE developed in partnership with The Princeton Review. These tools are designed to help students identify knowledge gaps and improve their study effectiveness.

The Gemini study notebooks allow students to upload materials, take diagnostic quizzes, and receive customized lesson plans that update based on their progress. Additionally, these notebooks integrate with NotebookLM for further study support. Google Classroom is also incorporating Gemini to provide safe, AI-driven learning experiences grounded in course materials, with features enabling teachers to assign personalized study notebooks and monitor student progress. These innovations aim to make learning more accessible and effective across various educational settings.

items.title: Google publishes white paper proposing a pragmatic, evidence-based approach to AI governance balancing safety and innovation in the US [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Read our white paper on a pragmatic approach to AI governance in America.
items.summary:
Google has released a white paper proposing a balanced, evidence-based approach to AI governance in the US that aims to avoid the extremes of over-regulation and no regulation. The paper suggests establishing an independent, federally overseen organization to set safety standards and conduct voluntary audits for advanced frontier AI models, while adapting existing laws to address social and economic impacts of widely used AI applications.

This approach seeks to protect public safety without hindering innovation, addressing challenges such as child safety, copyright, and workforce transitions. Google hopes this framework will contribute to ongoing discussions about effective AI regulation and ensure broad benefits from AI technologies.

This investment is part of a broader trend of global tech companies boosting their presence in India to support AI development, with Microsoft and Google also making significant commitments. The Indian government has encouraged such investments through policy incentives, aiming to establish the country as a major hub for AI and cloud computing infrastructure. Alongside infrastructure growth, Amazon is also expanding its retail and logistics operations to strengthen its position in India's competitive quick-commerce market.

items.title: Cloudflare releases Cloudflare One stack, an open-source library of AI agent skills for Zero Trust deployment and automated migration from Zscaler and Palo Alto Networks [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Cloudflare Ships Agent Skills for Zero Trust Deployment and Migration
items.summary:
Cloudflare has launched the Cloudflare One stack, an open-source library of AI agent skills designed to assist in planning, deploying, managing, and migrating Zero Trust environments. This library includes automated migration capabilities specifically for transitioning from Zscaler and Palo Alto Networks, using the same logic as Cloudflare's Descaler program, which has enabled rapid enterprise migrations.

The stack provides structured knowledge and decision trees that help AI agents handle tasks such as VPN replacement, user and network security, and connectivity management. It supports a review-before-apply workflow to ensure security teams maintain control over configuration changes. Available on GitHub, the Cloudflare One stack aims to streamline Zero Trust deployments and reduce manual effort for both customers and partners, with ongoing development of additional migration and troubleshooting skills.

items.title: FIFA offers AI agent to all teams at 2026 World Cup to level playing field amid concerns over resource disparities in AI tools and data analysis [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: World Cup Teams Are in a Race for AI Dominance
items.summary:
FIFA is providing all teams at the 2026 World Cup with access to a bespoke AI agent powered by Lenovo, aiming to level the playing field amid growing disparities in AI tools and data analysis capabilities. This initiative comes as the tournament will track an unprecedented volume of data, with around 150 million data points per match, to enhance team strategies and player performance.

While AI and data analytics have become integral to modern soccer, enabling detailed match analysis and tactical planning, the cost and expertise required to utilize these technologies remain a challenge for smaller or less wealthy nations. items.title: Slack details four-phase evolution of its AI serving platform from Amazon SageMaker to a multi-cloud architecture using AWS Bedrock and Google Cloud Vertex AI, improving performance and resilience [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Slack Outlines Four-Phase Journey to a Multi-Cloud AI Serving Platform
items.summary:
Slack has detailed the evolution of its AI serving platform through four phases, transitioning from a self-managed Amazon SageMaker setup to a multi-cloud architecture utilizing AWS Bedrock and Google Cloud Vertex AI. This shift improved performance, reducing latency by about 67% for short prompts and enhancing quality on complex reasoning tasks by around 10%. The multi-cloud approach also increased resilience and broadened access to diverse AI models.

Initially, Slack managed its AI infrastructure on Amazon SageMaker, which required manual capacity planning and posed challenges with GPU resource availability. Migrating to AWS Bedrock reduced operational overhead and improved access to newer models, while a hybrid capacity model balanced provisioned and on-demand throughput to handle traffic variability. To address dependency on a single provider, Slack integrated Google Cloud Vertex AI, creating a provider-agnostic serving layer with unified observability and intelligent routing to optimize performance and reliability.

This architecture not only enhanced Slack's AI capabilities but also offered improved geographic failover and reduced reliance on any single cloud platform. Slack's experience reflects a growing trend among companies to adopt multi-cloud AI strategies to ensure operational flexibility, resilience, and access to evolving model ecosystems.

items.title: WIRED investigation reveals British police built extensive crime-prediction system with unreliable results, leading to abandonment of some models and transparency concerns [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: British Police Built a Sprawling Crime-Prediction Machine. Some Results Couldn’t Be Trusted
items.summary:
A WIRED investigation has uncovered that Avon and Somerset Police in the UK developed an extensive crime-prediction system using machine-learning models that analyzed sensitive data from nearly half a million residents. The system included at least 23 models aimed at predicting risks such as burglary, court absences, and domestic abuse, but some models were later abandoned due to unreliable results and concerns over transparency.

The investigation revealed that the public was largely unaware of these predictive tools, with individuals like local activist John Pegram only learning about their inclusion years after the systems were implemented. Despite requests for information, the police have been reluctant to disclose details about how data is used or how risk scores are assigned. Independent reviews highlighted poor predictive performance and warned that the lack of transparency could erode public trust.

These findings come as the UK moves toward broader adoption of AI and predictive analytics in policing, with leaders like former Avon and Somerset Chief Constable Andy Marsh advocating for rapid integration of such technologies. The case raises important questions about accountability, data privacy, and the effectiveness of AI-driven crime prevention in law enforcement.

items.title: Immunologist Derya Unutmaz uses GPT-5 Pro to solve a 3-year-old T cell glucose metabolism mystery, advancing cancer and autoimmune research [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: How GPT-5 helped immunologist Derya Unutmaz solve a 3-year-old mystery
items.summary:
Immunologist Derya Unutmaz used GPT-5 Pro to solve a three-year-old puzzle about how glucose affects T cell development, a key question in immunology with implications for cancer and autoimmune disease research. The AI model helped identify that a glucose-like molecule, deoxyglucose, disrupts the production of a protein that normally prevents T cells from becoming inflammatory cells, explaining unexpected experimental results.

Unutmaz's team initially struggled to interpret their findings from 2022, but GPT-5 Pro provided insights that connected glucose metabolism to T cell specialization. The model also accurately predicted outcomes of related experiments, demonstrating its potential as a collaborative tool in scientific research. This breakthrough highlights how advanced AI can augment human expertise and accelerate understanding in complex biomedical fields.

The foundation seeks to create open, modular specifications that translate international standards into practical assessment criteria, fostering trust and cooperation among organizations and governments worldwide.

By promoting interoperable standards and trusted third-party assessments, the Appia Foundation aims to support coordinated responses to AI risks and facilitate global collaboration in managing the challenges posed by increasingly capable AI technologies.

items.title: Grab launches Palana, a Kubernetes-native secure execution platform to safely run autonomous AI agents with infrastructure-level isolation and dynamic secrets management [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.originalTitle: Grab Builds Secure Agentic AI Workload Platform
items.summary:
Grab has developed Palana, a Kubernetes-native secure execution platform designed to safely run autonomous AI agents by providing infrastructure-level isolation and dynamic secrets management. Palana addresses the security challenges posed by the unpredictable behaviors of model-driven AI agents, such as arbitrary tool use and code execution, by isolating each agent in dedicated Kubernetes namespaces with strict access controls and network policies.

The platform enhances security by separating sensitive credentials from the agent runtime, using a proxy to dynamically inject secrets only when needed, preventing exposure within the agent environment. Palana also centralizes outbound traffic through a secure proxy with real-time traffic inspection and policy enforcement, while operational controls like network kill switches and external reapers manage agent lifecycle independently from the agent code. This Kubernetes-native approach enables scalable, auditable, and manageable deployment of multiple autonomous AI workloads within a zero-trust framework.

items.title: Hasbro requires Peppa Pig child actors to sign contracts surrendering AI voice rights amid industry backlash [ * ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Peppa Pig Owner Demands Child Actors Sign Away Voice Rights to AI
items.summary:
Hasbro, the owner of the children’s series "Peppa Pig," is requiring child voice actors to sign contracts that surrender their rights to the use of their voices for artificial intelligence purposes. This move has sparked backlash from industry advocacy groups, who argue that children cannot provide fully informed consent for such agreements and that their voices should be exempt from AI usage. The Agents of Young Performers Association has led a public campaign opposing these contract terms, emphasizing the need for careful consent when it involves minors.

Hasbro has responded by stating its commitment to protecting child performers' rights and addressing AI-related concerns responsibly, though it declined to comment on specific contract negotiations. The controversy highlights broader industry tensions as studios increasingly seek to use AI technology in voice acting and animation, raising questions about the rights and protections of performers, especially children, in the evolving entertainment landscape.

items.title: Anthropic Claude Code lead argues HTML improves human-agent communication and engagement over Markdown in complex agentic workflows [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Anthropic Lead: HTML Increasingly Better Than Markdown at Keeping Humans Engaged in Agentic Loops
items.summary:
Thariq Shihipar, engineering lead for Anthropic's Claude Code team, argues that HTML enhances human-agent communication and engagement more effectively than Markdown in complex workflows. He highlights HTML's richer visualizations, interactivity, and color as key factors that improve productivity, especially in tasks involving goal communication, specification refinement, and output review.

Shihipar points out that as agent outputs grow longer and more complex, Markdown becomes restrictive and harder to read, leading to potential quality and maintenance issues if outputs are accepted without thorough review. He advocates for single-file HTML artifacts that create interactive, customized workspaces suited to various tasks such as code review, interface design, and data visualization. This perspective has sparked debate among developers, with some supporting HTML's advantages and others cautioning against losing Markdown's simplicity and security benefits.

items.title: SoftBank CEO Masayoshi Son calls AI bubble warnings blasphemy, defends $64 billion investment in OpenAI and says AI’s potential is just beginning [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Softbank CEO Who’s Invested $64 Billion in OpenAI Says It’s “Blasphemy” to Mention the AI Bubble
items.summary:
SoftBank CEO Masayoshi Son has dismissed concerns about an AI bubble as "blasphemy," defending the company's $64 billion investment in OpenAI and expressing strong confidence in AI's future potential. Speaking at SoftBank's annual general meeting, Son emphasized that AI's development is just beginning and compared the current AI revolution to being significantly larger than the dot-com boom of the late 1990s.

Despite Son's optimism, some SoftBank insiders have expressed unease about the massive investment, fearing it could backfire given OpenAI's high cash burn rate and operational challenges. Son acknowledged the possibility of market corrections but viewed them as opportunities for long-term growth, drawing parallels to historical recoveries after major economic crashes.

Omio aims to become fully AI-native by rethinking workflows across all functions, emphasizing responsible deployment throughout its AI integration.

items.title: Survey finds over half of US consumers avoid AI customer service agents and may switch brands after three minutes of automated interaction [ * ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Customers Are Ditching Companies That Force Them to Talk to an AI Agent
items.summary:
A recent survey by customer service AI company Parloa reveals that over half of U.S. consumers actively try to avoid interacting with AI customer service agents, with many willing to switch brands after just three minutes of automated interaction. The study found that frustration with bots that fail to understand users ranks higher than long hold times or multiple transfers, highlighting significant dissatisfaction with current AI service experiences.

Despite this, 85% of respondents expressed willingness to embrace automated systems if they reliably resolved issues, indicating potential for improvement. However, trust in AI handling complex requests remains low, with 30.4% expressing no trust at all. The findings underscore growing consumer exhaustion and impatience with ineffective AI customer service, signaling challenges for companies relying on automated agents to maintain brand loyalty.

items.title: DuckDuckGo’s AI search feature falsely claims Donald Trump died of rabies in June, citing misinformation spread on Reddit [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: DuckDuckGo’s AI Feature Is Telling Users That Trump Died of Rabies Earlier This Month
items.summary:
DuckDuckGo's AI search feature incorrectly claimed that former President Donald Trump died of rabies in June, citing false information that originated from Reddit. The AI also falsely reported that Vice President JD Vance had died from the same disease, a claim that is entirely untrue. These inaccuracies stem from misinformation spread by users on a subreddit dedicated to deliberately misleading AI systems.

The misinformation campaign involves Reddit users posting fabricated stories, including fake news articles and social media posts, to trick AI models into repeating false claims. This incident highlights the challenges AI systems face in verifying information and the risks of relying on unverified online content. DuckDuckGo acknowledged the error and stated it has taken steps to correct the issue and improve its AI's accuracy in handling such situations.

DuckDuckGo's AI search feature incorrectly claimed that former President Donald Trump died of rabies in June, citing false information that originated from Reddit. The AI also falsely reported that Vice President JD Vance had died from the same disease, a claim that is entirely untrue. These inaccuracies stem from misinformation spread by users on a subreddit dedicated to deliberately misleading AI systems.

The misinformation campaign involves Reddit users posting fabricated stories, including fake news articles and social media posts, to trick AI models into repeating false claims. This incident highlights the challenges AI systems face in verifying information and the risks of relying on unverified online content. DuckDuckGo acknowledged the error and stated it has taken steps to correct the issue and improve its AI's accuracy in handling such situations.

items.title: Google rolls out new Search Services History feature storing uploaded media for AI training by default; users can opt out via My Activity settings [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: How to Opt Out of Google Search’s New AI Data Training Feature
items.summary:
Google has introduced a new Search Services History feature that automatically stores media uploads, such as images and audio from user interactions, to train its AI models. This update is part of a global rollout and is enabled by default, though users can opt out through the My Activity settings by disabling the option to save media for AI training.

The stored media includes a wide range of content, from photos used in reverse image searches to voice recordings from Google Translate, and is retained for up to four years even if users delete the original activity. Google states that these settings aim to provide more relevant search results and allow users to revisit past searches, but the default opt-in approach has raised privacy concerns among experts who advocate for explicit user consent before data collection for AI training.

items.title: OpenAI and Broadcom announce Jalapeño chip for large language model inference, targeting data center deployment by end of 2026 [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: OpenAI and Broadcom announce chip designed for LLM inference at scale
items.summary:
OpenAI and Broadcom have jointly announced the development of a new chip called Jalapeño, designed specifically for large language model (LLM) inference in data centers. The chip aims to improve performance and efficiency for LLM workloads and is expected to be deployed in data centers by the end of 2026. This initiative represents the first generation of a long-term project to create specialized hardware tailored to OpenAI's future model requirements.

The Jalapeño chip was developed over nine months based on detailed insights from OpenAI's research and roadmap, with Broadcom designing the ASIC from scratch to meet the specific needs of LLM inference. Early testing suggests the chip will deliver better performance per watt compared to current state-of-the-art solutions, although detailed technical results are forthcoming. This collaboration reflects OpenAI's strategy to reduce reliance on external suppliers like Nvidia by vertically integrating its hardware and software stack amid growing demand for AI compute capacity.

items.title: OpenAI launches Patch the Planet with Trail of Bits to help open-source maintainers find and fix vulnerabilities using AI and expert review [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.originalTitle: Patch the Planet: a Daybreak initiative to support open source maintainers
items.summary:
OpenAI has launched Patch the Planet, a Daybreak initiative developed in collaboration with Trail of Bits to support open-source software maintainers in identifying and fixing security vulnerabilities. The program combines AI-assisted security research using advanced models with expert human review to validate issues and develop patches, aiming to reduce the workload on maintainers while enhancing software security.

Patch the Planet involves close collaboration with maintainers to tailor security efforts, including vulnerability validation, patch development, and continuous integration improvements. Initial participants include prominent projects such as cURL, the Go project, and Python, with Trail of Bits dedicating their security research team to investigate vulnerabilities, develop patches, and coordinate disclosures. The initiative also partners with HackerOne and Calif to extend vulnerability triage and coordinated disclosure efforts.

Early results from the program include the rapid creation of fuzzing labs and reusable pipelines for detecting variants of known vulnerabilities, significantly accelerating security research processes. These advancements demonstrate the potential of combining AI capabilities with expert oversight to strengthen the security of critical open-source infrastructure.

items.title: OpenAI launches Daybreak tools including Codex Security and GPT-5.5-Cyber to automate vulnerability discovery and patching for organizations worldwide [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.originalTitle: Daybreak: Tools for securing every organization in the world
items.summary:
OpenAI has launched Daybreak, a suite of tools including Codex Security and GPT-5.5-Cyber, designed to automate the discovery, validation, and patching of software vulnerabilities for organizations worldwide. These tools aim to accelerate end-to-end patch automation, helping defenders manage the increasing volume of vulnerabilities found by AI models.

Daybreak includes an updated Codex Security plugin that integrates lessons from internal and customer use to speed up vulnerability management and prevention. The full version of GPT-5.5-Cyber, now available to trusted defenders, improves performance on cybersecurity tasks. Additionally, the Daybreak Cyber Partner Program and the Patch the Planet initiative collaborate with open-source projects and security partners to scale these capabilities and ensure responsible access and oversight.

This initiative addresses the shift in cybersecurity where the bottleneck has moved from finding vulnerabilities to efficiently patching them. By democratizing access to advanced AI-driven security tools, OpenAI aims to empower organizations to protect critical infrastructure and software systems more effectively against evolving cyber threats.

items.title: A24 announces $75 million AI research partnership with Google DeepMind amid backlash from indie film fans [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: A24 Knows You’re Mad About the Google AI Collab
items.summary:
A24, the influential indie film studio known for hits like "Backrooms," has announced a $75 million research partnership with Google DeepMind to develop new AI filmmaking tools. This collaboration, part of A24's technology startup A24 Labs, aims to give artists a role in shaping AI-driven creative workflows. The announcement has sparked backlash among A24's dedicated fanbase, who view the move as contradictory to the studio's indie ethos and have expressed their discontent on social media.

The partnership reflects a broader trend of AI companies increasing their presence in Hollywood, raising concerns about AI's impact on creative jobs and the film industry. While some studios have embraced AI investments, others have faced criticism and legal challenges over copyright issues. A24 emphasizes that the collaboration is a research effort intended to influence the development of AI tools rather than passively adopting existing technologies, seeking to maintain a voice for artists in the evolving landscape.

items.title: Rep. Anna Paulina Luna says staff used AI only for spellcheck in defense bill amendment summary, denies AI drafted any legislation text [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Congresswoman denies staff used AI to write defense funding amendment
items.summary:
Rep. Anna Paulina Luna (R-FL) clarified that her staff used AI solely for spellchecking an amendment summary related to the 2027 National Defense Authorization Act, denying that AI was involved in drafting the actual legislative text. She emphasized that all official bill text originates from the House Legislative Council, which is prohibited from using AI in its drafting process. Luna's statement came after social media users shared screenshots suggesting AI involvement in the amendment's content.

Initially, Luna's comments implied AI might have been used to correct draft text, but she later corrected her statement to specify that AI was only used for spell and grammar checks on the summary, not the amendment itself. This incident highlights ongoing concerns and discussions about the role of AI tools in legislative and legal work, as similar cases have emerged involving AI-generated legal documents and legislation in other jurisdictions.

items.title: Uber, DoorDash, and Cloudflare expand AI use from code review to product requirement document governance, adding early-stage validation and multi-agent analysis in software development [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: AI Is Moving up the Software Lifecycle: from Code Review to PRD Governance
items.summary:
Technology companies Uber, DoorDash, and Cloudflare are expanding the use of artificial intelligence beyond code generation and review to earlier stages of software development, such as product requirement document (PRD) validation and design input evaluation. These initiatives introduce AI as a governance layer that assesses engineering artifacts before implementation, aiming to improve clarity, completeness, and risk identification while maintaining human oversight.

Uber's AI system reviews PRDs to highlight missing dependencies and unclear assumptions before engineering teams begin work. DoorDash employs an AI-powered code reviewer that provides actionable, context-aware feedback integrated into existing workflows to enhance review efficiency without increasing noise. Cloudflare uses a multi-agent AI approach, assigning specialized tasks like security and performance analysis to different agents, which collectively improve the precision and relevance of code reviews.

These developments reflect a shift toward continuous, AI-assisted validation throughout the software lifecycle, supporting human decision-making and enhancing the quality and reliability of software engineering processes.

items.title: VC partner says veteran software engineers face identity crisis and burnout fixing poor AI-generated code amid rising AI tool usage in tech companies [ * ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Software Engineers Are Facing an Existential Crisis As They Drown In Horrendous AI Code
items.summary:
Veteran software engineers are experiencing an identity crisis and burnout as they struggle to fix poor-quality code generated by AI tools, according to Deedy Das, a partner at Menlo Ventures. The rapid adoption of AI in tech companies has created a divide between less experienced coders relying heavily on AI and seasoned engineers who must correct the resulting errors, leading to frustration and declining morale.

This trend is exacerbated by workplace pressures to use AI extensively, with some companies incorporating AI usage into performance evaluations. The phenomenon, sometimes called "tokenmaxxing," encourages excessive AI reliance, which often produces subpar outputs that require correction by more skilled engineers. This dynamic has led to increased workloads, rising animosity among colleagues, and a sense of disillusionment among veteran engineers who feel their craft is being undermined.

Krugman's comments underscore the complex relationship between AI innovation, economic disruption, and societal response.

Bores, known for coauthoring the RAISE Act that imposed AI safety regulations, gained national attention after pro-AI super PACs funded by Anthropic-backed groups supported his campaign, while OpenAI-backed PACs opposed him. Despite the significant spending, local political dynamics and endorsements played a decisive role in the outcome.

The race highlighted the growing influence of AI industry interests in political campaigns, with multiple super PACs spending millions to sway the election as a test case for AI regulation debates ahead of the midterms. Bores's close finish demonstrated public readiness to challenge powerful AI companies, though the general election is expected to focus on broader issues including party alignments and other national concerns. items.title: Oracle lays off 21,000 employees amid $45 billion debt-funded AI data center expansion for fiscal year 2026 [ ! ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Oracle’s 21,000 layoffs help drive its debt-fueled AI investments
items.summary:
Oracle has laid off 21,000 employees, reducing its workforce by nearly 13% over the past year, as part of a restructuring plan linked to its significant investment in AI and cloud infrastructure. The company plans to raise $45 billion to $50 billion, primarily through debt, to expand its data centers and support AI workloads for clients such as OpenAI and Meta. This move reflects Oracle's strategic shift toward AI-driven cloud services amid growing industry reliance on artificial intelligence technologies.

The layoffs coincide with Oracle's increased capital expenditures and a rise in restructuring costs, which reached $1.8 billion in the fiscal year ending May 31. Oracle acknowledged potential challenges from the workforce reduction, including impacts on productivity and employee morale, but emphasized its commitment to balancing resources to deliver advanced cloud and AI products. The company's growing debt and dependence on AI customers have raised concerns among investors and bondholders, highlighting the financial risks associated with its aggressive AI expansion.

items.title: Google advances AI-powered natural disaster forecasting and real-time alerts to improve global crisis resilience and reduce surprise from extreme weather events [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Towards a world where no one is surprised by a natural disaster
items.summary:
Google is advancing AI-powered technologies to improve natural disaster forecasting and provide real-time alerts, aiming to enhance global crisis resilience and reduce unexpected impacts from extreme weather events. Building on a decade of research, Google has developed models that predict floods, wildfires, earthquakes, and extreme weather with greater accuracy and lead time, reaching billions of people worldwide through its platforms.

Key innovations include a global flood forecasting model covering over 150 countries, AI-based wildfire boundary tracking in 34 countries, and the WeatherNext 2 system for detailed cyclone predictions. Google also collaborates with partners to deploy satellite constellations for wildfire detection and uses AI to help cities mitigate extreme heat. These efforts are integrated into Google Search, Maps, and public alert systems to deliver timely, authoritative crisis information to users and emergency responders.

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-5.5 Instant with improved health intelligence, physician-led evaluations, and 71% fewer factuality issues in ChatGPT health responses [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Improving health intelligence in ChatGPT
items.summary:
OpenAI has launched GPT-5.5 Instant, an enhanced version of ChatGPT that significantly improves health and wellness responses by incorporating physician-led evaluations and advanced reasoning capabilities. This update reduces factual inaccuracies by 71% in health-related interactions and offers clearer communication, better context awareness, and more accurate guidance on when urgent care is needed. GPT-5.5 Instant is now available to all free ChatGPT users, making these improvements widely accessible.

The development of GPT-5.5 Instant involved collaboration with a global network of physicians who helped define quality standards and assess model responses using health-specific evaluations like HealthBench Professional. Compared to previous versions and even physician-written responses, GPT-5.5 Instant demonstrated superior accuracy, safety, and completeness in handling complex health queries. Monitoring of production traffic further confirms the model's enhanced reliability in real-world health conversations.

These advancements enable ChatGPT to better assist users in understanding medical information, preparing for appointments, and making informed decisions about their health. By recognizing uncertainty and the need for additional context, GPT-5.5 Instant provides more trustworthy and useful health advice, reflecting a meaningful step forward in AI-driven health intelligence.

items.title: OpenAI researchers use AI reasoning model to identify 18 new diagnoses in 376 previously unsolved rare childhood genetic disease cases [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Using AI to help physicians diagnose rare genetic diseases affecting children
items.summary:
Researchers from Boston Children’s Hospital, Harvard University, and OpenAI used an OpenAI reasoning model to reanalyze 376 previously unsolved rare childhood genetic disease cases, identifying 18 new diagnoses. The model generated evidence-linked hypotheses that experts reviewed, leading to confirmed diagnoses in cases that had eluded years of specialist analysis. This study, published in NEJM AI, demonstrates how AI-assisted workflows can enhance diagnostic yield by revisiting difficult cases as scientific knowledge evolves.

The team provided the model with de-identified clinical and genomic data, including phenotype descriptions and variant information, and asked it to propose plausible molecular explanations with justifications. Experts then applied established clinical frameworks to evaluate the model’s outputs, confirming diagnoses through additional testing and clinical validation. This approach highlights the potential for scalable, periodic reanalysis of rare disease cases to improve diagnostic outcomes as new gene-disease relationships and variant classifications emerge.

items.originalTitle: A near-autonomous AI chemist improves a challenging reaction in medicinal chemistry
items.summary:
OpenAI and Molecule.one collaborated to develop a near-autonomous AI chemist powered by GPT-5.4 that significantly improved the Chan-Lam coupling reaction for primary sulfonamides, a key process in medicinal chemistry. The AI system, integrated with Molecule.one's high-throughput laboratory, autonomously designed and conducted experiments, identifying additives that boosted reaction yields for the majority of tested substrates.

This advancement addresses a longstanding challenge in drug discovery, where low yields in synthesizing certain molecules limit exploration and development. By enhancing the reliability and efficiency of this reaction, the AI-driven approach offers medicinal chemists a more practical method to produce important compounds, potentially accelerating the creation of new therapeutics across various medical fields.

items.originalTitle: Introducing LifeSciBench
items.summary:
OpenAI has launched LifeSciBench, a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate AI systems on their ability to perform complex, real-world life science research tasks. Developed and reviewed by Ph.D.-level scientists with industry experience, LifeSciBench includes 750 expert-authored tasks across seven workflows and biological domains, reflecting the multifaceted nature of scientific research beyond simple fact recall.

The benchmark assesses AI performance on tasks such as interpreting evidence, designing experiments, and making research decisions under uncertainty, using detailed rubrics with over 19,000 criteria to evaluate scientific accuracy and reasoning. LifeSciBench incorporates diverse data artifacts and emphasizes multi-step reasoning, aiming to measure how well AI can support practical life science workflows and contribute meaningfully to drug discovery and related fields.

items.title: Google DeepMind outlines AI Control Roadmap combining traditional safeguards and real-time monitoring to secure internal AI agents against misalignment and threats [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
items.originalTitle: Securing the future of AI agents
items.summary:
Google DeepMind has introduced an AI Control Roadmap designed to secure internal AI agents by combining traditional cybersecurity measures with real-time monitoring and model alignment techniques. This framework treats AI agents as potentially misaligned, implementing a layered defense system that includes threat modeling, continuous supervision by trusted AI systems, and incremental permission granting based on verified behavior.

The roadmap builds on established cybersecurity practices and adapts them to the unique challenges posed by advanced AI, such as the potential for agents to evade detection or cause harm. It emphasizes scalable security protocols that adjust according to the AI's capabilities, ensuring both asynchronous and real-time responses to mitigate risks effectively. This approach aims to provide robust safeguards as AI systems become more capable and integrated into critical tasks.

items.originalTitle: Predicting model behavior before release by simulating deployment
items.summary:
OpenAI has introduced Deployment Simulation, a new method that predicts how AI models will behave before they are released by replaying real conversation data with candidate models. This approach helps identify potential safety risks and undesired behaviors in realistic contexts, improving the accuracy of pre-deployment evaluations.

Deployment Simulation addresses limitations of traditional testing by using recent deployment conversations to simulate model responses, reducing biases and increasing coverage of possible behaviors. It has been applied successfully to GPT-5-series models and complex agentic rollouts, providing valuable insights that inform safety measures and deployment decisions. OpenAI plans to expand the use of this method to enhance future model development and risk assessment processes.

items.title: OpenAI launches Partner Network with $150M investment to accelerate global enterprise AI adoption and train 300,000 certified consultants by end of 2026 [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Introducing the OpenAI Partner Network
items.summary:
OpenAI has launched the Partner Network, a new program designed to accelerate enterprise AI adoption worldwide by collaborating with trusted partners who have deep industry expertise and global delivery capabilities. The company is investing $150 million to support this initiative and aims to train 300,000 certified consultants by the end of 2026 to help organizations effectively integrate AI into their operations.

The Partner Network enables partners to build, sell, and deploy AI solutions using OpenAI's technology, offering a tiered system that recognizes partners' sales performance, technical skills, and deployment experience. This program also includes specializations in key areas like cybersecurity and coding, and a pilot Forward Deployed Experts program to provide enhanced support for complex enterprise deployments.

By fostering a robust ecosystem of partners, OpenAI seeks to help enterprises move from AI ambition to measurable outcomes through strategic use case identification, workflow redesign, secure integration, and change management. Early collaborations with companies such as Agilent, eBay, Paychex, and T-Mobile demonstrate the network's potential to drive significant improvements in customer service, operational efficiency, and AI-enabled experiences.

items.title: OpenAI launches three new Academy courses to teach practical AI skills, workflows, and agent use for workplace applications [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: New OpenAI Academy courses for the next era of work
items.summary:
OpenAI has launched three new courses on its Academy platform designed to help individuals and organizations develop practical AI skills and integrate AI tools into their daily work. The courses—AI Foundations, Applied AI Foundations, and Agents and Workflows—guide learners from understanding basic AI concepts to creating repeatable workflows and managing agent-assisted tasks.

These courses are developed in collaboration with partners like BCG, Accenture, and BBVA, and focus on hands-on learning tailored to real work scenarios. They aim to build AI fluency across teams, enabling users to improve routine tasks, design structured workflows, and apply AI responsibly and effectively in the workplace.

OpenAI Academy also offers certificates upon course completion to recognize progress and encourage knowledge sharing within organizations. The initiative supports enterprises in scaling AI adoption by providing a consistent, evolving curriculum aligned with OpenAI’s latest technologies and safety practices.

items.title: Preply launches OpenAI-powered Lesson Insights to generate AI-driven personalized feedback and exercises for language learners [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: How Preply combines AI and human tutors to personalize learning
items.summary:
Preply, the world's largest online language learning marketplace, has launched Lesson Insights, an AI-powered feature using OpenAI technology to generate personalized lesson summaries, feedback, and exercises for language learners. This tool analyzes lesson transcripts to provide tailored guidance on grammar, vocabulary, and pronunciation, enhancing the learning experience while reducing tutors' administrative workload.

Lesson Insights integrates seamlessly into Preply's platform, delivering detailed reports to both tutors and students shortly after each session. These insights support continuous learning by informing personalized homework and practice, helping learners track progress and stay motivated. Preply's adoption of OpenAI extends beyond this feature, with AI tools embedded across the company to improve operations and content creation.

items.title: Astrophysicist Chi-kwan Chan uses OpenAI Codex to develop and test algorithms simulating plasma behavior around black holes, aiding Event Horizon Telescope research [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: How an astrophysicist uses Codex to help simulate black holes
items.summary:
Astrophysicist Chi-kwan Chan uses OpenAI's Codex to develop and test new algorithms that simulate the behavior of plasma around black holes, enhancing the realism of models used by the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) collaboration. These simulations help scientists study extreme physics near black holes and support efforts to produce the first video of a supermassive black hole.

Chan's work addresses challenges in modeling plasma particles that spiral around magnetic fields near black holes, where traditional simulations require immense computing power due to the need to track tiny particle motions. By leveraging Codex to explore and validate novel mathematical approaches, Chan aims to overcome these limitations and improve the accuracy and efficiency of black hole simulations.

This approach allows researchers to better interpret observational data and test fundamental theories like Einstein's general relativity. While AI-generated algorithms require rigorous testing, Chan emphasizes that scientific validation remains essential, and AI tools like Codex offer promising support for advancing astrophysical research.

items.title: OpenAI supports EU Code of Practice on AI content transparency, advancing provenance standards and tools for trustworthy AI ecosystem [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Supporting Europe’s work in ensuring a trustworthy AI ecosystem
items.summary:
OpenAI has announced its support for the European Union's Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content, aiming to enhance provenance standards and tools that help users understand AI-created content. This initiative aligns with the EU AI Act and reflects OpenAI's ongoing commitment to building a trustworthy AI ecosystem through transparency and cooperation with industry stakeholders.

OpenAI has been advancing provenance methods since 2024, incorporating C2PA metadata and SynthID watermarks in its AI-generated images, and providing public verification tools. The company collaborates with cross-industry groups to develop interoperable standards and employs a multi-layered approach combining metadata, watermarking, and product safeguards to ensure content authenticity and reduce misuse.

The support for the Code of Practice underscores the importance of reliable provenance in combating disinformation and maintaining digital trust. OpenAI emphasizes that transparency efforts require ecosystem-wide collaboration to improve the robustness and interoperability of provenance techniques as AI-generated content becomes more prevalent.

items.title: Google DeepMind releases DiffusionGemma, a 26B MoE model offering up to 4x faster text generation on GPUs with bi-directional attention and iterative self-correction [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: DiffusionGemma: 4x faster text generation
items.summary:
Google DeepMind has introduced DiffusionGemma, a 26 billion parameter Mixture of Experts (MoE) model designed for significantly faster text generation on GPUs. Unlike traditional autoregressive models that generate text token-by-token, DiffusionGemma produces entire blocks of text simultaneously, achieving up to four times faster inference speeds. This model features bi-directional attention and iterative self-correction, enabling it to refine outputs in real-time and handle complex tasks such as in-line editing and code infilling more effectively.

DiffusionGemma operates efficiently on consumer-grade GPUs by activating only a subset of its parameters during inference, fitting within 18GB of VRAM when quantized. While it offers speed advantages for interactive and local workflows, its output quality is lower than that of standard Gemma 4 models, which remain recommended for high-quality production use. The model's diffusion-based approach shifts the computational bottleneck from memory bandwidth to processing power, making it particularly suited for low-latency applications where rapid text generation is critical.

items.title: OpenAI reports PRC-linked influence operations using AI-generated content to target US AI policy debates and data center narratives in 2026 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: PRC-linked influence operations are targeting AI debates in the US
items.summary:
OpenAI has reported that influence operations linked to the People's Republic of China used AI-generated content to interfere in U.S. debates on artificial intelligence policy and technology infrastructure. These operations involved two main campaigns: one spreading claims that AI data center expansions were driving up electricity costs for families, and another criticizing U.S. tariffs while falsely alleging that ChatGPT user data had been compromised.

The campaigns sought to covertly influence public opinion by exploiting existing concerns about energy prices and technology competition, while avoiding direct references to Chinese leadership. OpenAI banned the involved accounts and emphasized that these efforts aimed to manipulate democratic discussions and test narratives around critical AI infrastructure, though there was no evidence of significant impact beyond the operators' own activity.

By disclosing these findings, OpenAI aims to assist governments, industry, and civil society in recognizing and countering foreign attempts to undermine democratic processes and promote authoritarian control through AI-based influence tactics.

items.title: Google DeepMind and partners announce $10M funding call for multi-agent AI safety research, inviting global proposals by August 2026 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Investing in multi-agent AI safety research
items.summary:
Google DeepMind, along with partners Schmidt Sciences, the Cooperative AI Foundation, ARIA, and Google.org, has announced a $10 million funding call to support global research on multi-agent AI safety. This initiative aims to address the challenges posed by the interaction of millions of AI agents across digital environments, focusing on understanding and mitigating risks that arise when independent AI systems communicate and operate together.

The funding targets research in four key areas: developing realistic test environments, studying the behavior of agent networks, enhancing secure agent infrastructure, and improving oversight and control mechanisms. Proposals are invited from academic and independent researchers worldwide, with applications open until August 2026 and awardees expected to be announced in autumn 2026. This effort seeks to build a safer and more stable AI ecosystem as multi-agent systems become increasingly prevalent.

items.title: LSEG deploys OpenAI tools to scale trusted AI across 4,000 employees, cutting product release cycles from six months to two weeks and accelerating customer delivery [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: From data to decisions: how LSEG is scaling trusted AI
items.summary:
London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG) has integrated OpenAI's generative AI tools across its global operations, enabling around 4,000 employees to accelerate product development and customer delivery. This deployment has reduced product release cycles from approximately six months to two weeks and shortened the time from customer request to production deployment to about four weeks. LSEG's adoption of OpenAI technology supports faster insight generation, improved collaboration, and enhanced innovation within one of the world's most complex financial data ecosystems.

LSEG's approach involved embedding governance and security measures while empowering teams to rethink workflows and leverage AI for tasks such as report drafting, market data synthesis, and rapid prototyping. The initiative has led to increased analyst productivity and a cultural shift toward faster, more creative problem-solving. By aligning with customer demand and integrating AI into existing workflows, LSEG has positioned itself to deliver trusted AI solutions at scale, transforming how financial data is utilized internally and by clients.

items.title: Google launches Gemini 3.5 Live Translate for near real-time speech translation in over 70 languages across Google AI Studio, Translate, and Meet [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Fluid, natural voice translation with Gemini 3.5 Live Translate
items.summary:
Google has introduced Gemini 3.5 Live Translate, a new audio model that enables near real-time speech-to-speech translation in over 70 languages. This technology is integrated into Google AI Studio, Google Translate, and Google Meet, offering smooth, natural-sounding translations that maintain the speaker's intonation and pacing without awkward pauses.

The model continuously generates speech during conversations, staying just seconds behind the speaker to provide fluid audio. It supports multilingual inputs without manual configuration and is designed to work well in noisy environments. Gemini 3.5 Live Translate is available to developers via the Gemini Live API, in private preview for Google Meet enterprise users, and broadly through the Google Translate app on Android and iOS, enhancing live interpretation for calls, meetings, and broadcasts.

items.title: Google DeepMind introduces Gemma 4 12B, a unified encoder-free multimodal model with native audio input and laptop-ready efficiency [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Introducing Gemma 4 12B: a unified, encoder-free multimodal model
items.summary:
Google DeepMind has introduced Gemma 4 12B, a new unified, encoder-free multimodal model designed to deliver advanced multimodal intelligence directly on laptops. This model supports native audio input and offers high-performance reasoning capabilities comparable to larger models, while maintaining a compact size that runs efficiently on devices with just 16GB of VRAM or unified memory. Released under an Apache 2.0 license, Gemma 4 12B aims to make powerful multimodal AI accessible and practical for a wide range of applications.

Gemma 4 12B features a novel architecture that eliminates separate multimodal encoders by integrating vision and audio inputs directly into the language model backbone. This approach reduces latency and memory usage, enabling faster and more efficient processing. The model replaces traditional vision encoders with a lightweight embedding module and projects raw audio signals into the same space as text tokens, streamlining multimodal input handling.

Developers can access Gemma 4 12B through various platforms and tools, including LM Studio, Ollama, and Google AI Edge apps, with pre-trained weights available on Hugging Face and Kaggle. The release also includes a Skills Repository to support agentic development and integration options for deployment on Google Cloud, facilitating versatile use cases from local inference to enterprise applications.

items.summary:
Google DeepMind has launched a three-month accelerator program to support 15 early-stage robotics startups across Europe. The program offers intensive mentorship, technical support, and access to advanced AI models to help these companies integrate artificial intelligence into their products and scale real-world applications. The selected startups work in diverse fields including healthcare, manufacturing, climate solutions, and logistics.

Participants in the accelerator receive hands-on guidance from Google DeepMind and Google experts, leveraging Google's AI stack and robotics models to transform cutting-edge research into practical robotic technologies. This initiative aims to advance the development of physical AI, enabling intelligent machines to interact more effectively and safely with the real world, addressing significant challenges through innovative robotics solutions.

items.title: Google DeepMind reports AI-powered Gemini Guided Learning boosted math scores by up to 2.5 years in eight-week Sierra Leone trial involving 1,763 students [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Measuring the impact of learning with AI in Sierra Leone and beyond
items.summary:
Google DeepMind conducted a randomized controlled trial in Sierra Leone involving 1,763 junior secondary students to evaluate the impact of its AI-powered Gemini Guided Learning feature on math progress. Over eight weeks, students using Guided Learning showed significant improvements, with math scores increasing by up to 2.5 years of typical learning progress compared to a control group. The trial demonstrated high student engagement and a shift toward deeper conceptual understanding rather than simply seeking answers.

The study emphasized the role of teachers in facilitating AI-supported learning, with educators designing lessons and guiding classroom discussions. Teachers also reported professional growth through the use of Gemini, which helped them explain concepts more effectively. The trial's results suggest that AI can augment teaching by promoting critical thinking and active learning, rather than replacing educators.

DeepMind plans to conduct further trials globally to build a comprehensive evidence base on AI's impact in education. They are also releasing resources to help others implement similar AI-driven learning programs and are committed to advancing responsible AI development in education through ongoing research and collaboration.

OpenAI stresses the importance of public coordination and international cooperation to manage risks and guide the development of AI technologies responsibly, aiming to prevent concentration of power and promote shared prosperity.

Endava, a global technology services company, is transforming its software delivery by integrating OpenAI's ChatGPT Enterprise and Codex into its workflows. The company developed DavaFlow, an AI-native delivery methodology that embeds OpenAI technology throughout the software lifecycle, from planning to deployment. Beyond engineering, AI tools are used by legal, finance, and operations teams to streamline tasks such as research, reporting, and project coordination, fostering a culture where AI is integral to daily work.

Endava emphasizes behavior change and leadership involvement in AI adoption, encouraging experimentation and early inclusion of non-technical teams. Looking ahead, the company aims to advance enterprise AI by orchestrating models, agents, and workflows to create integrated systems that redefine organizational operations.

items.originalTitle: Dreaming: Better memory for a more helpful ChatGPT
items.summary:
OpenAI has launched Dreaming V3, an advanced memory system for ChatGPT Plus and Pro users in the US, designed to enhance the model's ability to retain context, track user preferences, and maintain relevance across conversations. This new system builds on previous memory features by synthesizing information from multiple interactions to provide fresher and more accurate responses without relying solely on explicit memory commands.

Dreaming V3 improves upon earlier versions by automatically curating and updating memories in the background, allowing ChatGPT to better understand ongoing user needs and preferences over time. Users can review and manage their stored memories through a summary page, enabling more personalized and context-aware interactions. The update aims to make ChatGPT more helpful by remembering useful details and adapting to changes, with plans to expand availability to more users and regions in the coming weeks.

items.originalTitle: Biodefense in the Intelligence Age
items.summary:
OpenAI has launched a biodefense action plan centered around its advanced AI model, GPT-Rosalind, to enhance biological threat detection and pandemic preparedness. Introduced in April 2026, GPT-Rosalind supports research in biology, drug discovery, and medicine, aiming to improve health outcomes by accelerating scientific understanding and therapy development.

Recognizing the dual-use nature of these AI capabilities, OpenAI announced Rosalind Biodefense in May 2026 to empower trusted developers in building biodefense tools while emphasizing responsible use and governance. The action plan seeks to create a more resilient biological future by enabling earlier threat detection, faster countermeasure development, and more coordinated crisis responses.

items.summary:
OpenAI has released an updated version of GPT-Rosalind, a model designed specifically for life sciences research. The new update integrates GPT-5.5’s advanced coding and tool-use abilities with enhanced expertise in medicinal chemistry, genomics, and broader biological analysis, improving performance across drug discovery and experimental workflows.

The update was evaluated using LifeSciBench, a benchmark developed to assess models on comprehensive life sciences tasks including evidence handling, scientific reasoning, and experimental validation. GPT-Rosalind demonstrated significant gains in addressing complex research challenges, such as analyzing clinical trial data and supporting drug development decisions, and is now available for research preview to qualified organizations worldwide.

OpenAI has released a blueprint proposing a federal framework for the governance of frontier AI in the United States, emphasizing safety, resilience, and national security. The plan suggests building on existing state laws and strengthening the role of the Center for AI Safety and Innovation (CAISI) as the primary federal institution overseeing AI safety. It also calls for a coordinated government-wide approach to address the challenges posed by advanced AI technologies.

The blueprint comes at a time when several states, including California, New York, and Illinois, have enacted frontier AI safety laws, and the White House has issued an executive order promoting AI innovation and security. OpenAI's proposal aims to create durable institutions capable of evolving alongside AI advancements to ensure responsible development and deployment.

items.summary:
Travelers has launched an AI-powered Claim Assistant nationwide, developed with OpenAI's Realtime API and advanced models, to provide customers with 24/7 support for filing auto property damage claims. The assistant guides users through the claims process using natural conversation, answers policy questions, and submits claims autonomously, helping Travelers manage high volumes during peak demand and catastrophe events.

Initially deployed in eight states, the AI Claim Assistant was expanded across the country within two months, with 85–90% of customers completing their claims through the system. This solution enables immediate customer assistance without wait times while allowing claim professionals to focus on complex cases, enhancing operational efficiency and customer experience at scale.

items.title: OpenAI calls for global AI Safety Institute to enhance youth protections and opportunities ahead of G7 Leaders’ Summit in June 2026 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Advancing youth safety and opportunity through global leadership
items.summary:
OpenAI has proposed the creation of a global AI Safety Institute aimed at enhancing protections and opportunities for young people as artificial intelligence becomes increasingly integrated into education and daily life. This initiative, highlighted ahead of the G7 Leaders’ Summit in June 2026, seeks to establish international collaboration to develop consistent safety standards, share research, and provide practical guidance for youth AI use.

The proposed institute would build on existing efforts like Common Sense Media’s Youth AI Safety Institute and partnerships with educators and researchers, including projects in Estonia and the United States. OpenAI emphasizes the importance of age-appropriate safeguards, regular risk assessments, parental controls, and transparent communication about AI’s benefits and risks to ensure safe and supportive AI experiences for young users.

OpenAI plans to work with governments, civil society, academia, and industry partners to promote sustained global leadership on youth AI safety, aiming to maintain momentum beyond the G7 summit and adapt to the evolving technological landscape.

items.title: OpenAI breaks ground on 1GW data center in Michigan with community partnerships, creating over 2,500 union construction jobs and investing $10 million in local projects [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: Building the infrastructure for the Intelligence Age in Michigan
items.summary:
OpenAI has begun construction on The Barn, a 1GW data center campus in Saline, Michigan, as part of its Stargate project to build AI infrastructure. The initiative aims to expand AI access, create over 2,500 union construction jobs, and invest $10 million in local community projects, including improvements to the Saline Recreation Center. The project also promises to protect local resources and prevent increased costs for local residents.

The data center will use a closed-loop cooling system to minimize water use and will not pass infrastructure costs onto local ratepayers. OpenAI is partnering with local organizations and government officials, including Governor Gretchen Whitmer, to ensure the project supports Michigan's workforce through union jobs and apprenticeship programs. Additionally, OpenAI plans to provide up to $45 million in Codex credits to eligible Michigan students to enhance AI literacy and workforce training.

This development is part of a broader effort to foster economic growth and technological leadership in Michigan, supporting local schools and services through projected tax revenues of $1 billion over the lease term. The project reflects a commitment to building AI infrastructure responsibly while investing in the communities that host it.

items.originalTitle: OpenAI frontier models and Codex are now available on AWS
items.summary:
OpenAI's frontier models and Codex are now generally available on AWS, enabling enterprises to integrate advanced AI capabilities within their existing AWS security, governance, and procurement frameworks. This availability allows organizations to accelerate AI adoption by using familiar AWS environments to move from evaluation to production more efficiently.

The integration includes OpenAI models and Codex on Amazon Bedrock, providing tools for AI application development and software engineering within AWS's secure infrastructure. Customers like Amgen and Autodesk highlight the benefits of this approach for accelerating workflows and maintaining high standards of accuracy and security.

Looking ahead, OpenAI and AWS plan to expand these offerings, including the upcoming Daybreak platform designed to enhance cybersecurity through AI-driven code review and threat detection. This collaboration aims to help more organizations deploy advanced AI solutions securely and effectively within their existing operational frameworks.

items.title: Boston Children’s Hospital uses OpenAI-powered AI to diagnose over 40 rare diseases and save 60,000 operational hours, redeploying $7 million in labor [ ! ] [ ⬢ ]
items.originalTitle: Boston Children’s uses AI to unlock new diagnoses
items.summary:
Boston Children’s Hospital has integrated OpenAI-powered artificial intelligence into its clinical and operational workflows to enhance patient care, reduce costs, and improve efficiency. This implementation has enabled the hospital to diagnose over 40 rare diseases that were previously unresolved, save approximately 60,000 operational hours, and redeploy more than $7 million in labor through over 50 AI-driven automations.

The hospital developed an enterprise AI layer, a secure internal ChatGPT environment, to support various teams including clinical, research, and administrative staff. This system helps synthesize complex medical data, streamline scheduling, and automate routine tasks, allowing staff to focus on higher-value work. The AI tools have been embedded across the organization to meet specific needs, resulting in faster innovation cycles and broader adoption among employees.

By leveraging AI for both operational improvements and clinical discovery, Boston Children’s has significantly advanced its capacity to diagnose rare diseases and optimize resource allocation. The approach demonstrates how AI can be effectively integrated into healthcare infrastructure to address cognitive limits and operational challenges while improving patient outcomes.

items.title: OpenAI shares guidance on designing trustworthy third-party AI evaluations for frontier model capabilities and safeguards [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: A shared playbook for trustworthy third party evaluations
items.summary:
OpenAI has published guidance on designing trustworthy third-party evaluations for frontier AI models, focusing on assessing capabilities, safeguards, and the validity of results. The guidance emphasizes the importance of clearly defining the claims being tested and providing evidence to support the evaluation's validity, especially as models now operate within complex environments using tools and multi-step workflows.

The guidance outlines different types of claims—capability elicitation, safeguard performance, and model comparison—and stresses the role of the evaluation setup, or "harness," in influencing performance outcomes. It also highlights common validity concerns such as reward hacking, refusals, contamination, broken problems, and sandbagging, recommending transparency about these factors to improve the reliability and usefulness of evaluation reports.

The guidance emphasizes the importance of clearly defining the claims being tested and providing evidence to support the evaluation's validity, especially as models now operate within complex environments using tools and multi-step workflows.

The guidance outlines different types of claims—capability elicitation, safeguard performance, and model comparison—and stresses the role of the evaluation setup, or "harness," in influencing performance outcomes. It also highlights common validity concerns such as reward hacking, refusals, contamination, broken problems, and sandbagging, recommending transparency about these factors to improve the reliability and usefulness of evaluation reports.

items.title: Endava uses Codex to codify senior engineering expertise and accelerate software delivery, reducing requirements analysis from weeks to hours across global teams [ * ] [ ◼ ]
items.originalTitle: How Endava builds an agentic organization with Codex
items.summary:
Endava, a global software contracting firm, leverages Codex to codify senior engineering expertise and accelerate its software delivery process, significantly reducing requirements analysis from weeks to hours. By integrating Codex across the entire delivery lifecycle, Endava has transformed into an agentic organization where senior knowledge guides teams in real time, enhancing collaboration and output quality.

Codex enables junior developers to produce senior-level work by providing architectural guidance and best practices, effectively scaling mentorship and expertise across global teams. This approach compresses traditionally sequential stages like analysis, design, and build into a unified process, improving efficiency and client engagement through live documentation and rapid iteration.

Endava's experience highlights the value of embedding senior judgment into AI tools to amplify team capabilities and streamline workflows beyond coding, including requirements analysis and client communication. Their success suggests that adopting such AI-driven methods can unlock substantial productivity gains in software development.

items.title: OpenAI publishes Frontier Governance Framework detailing AI safety and security practices aligned with emerging EU and California regulations [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: OpenAI’s Frontier Governance Framework
items.summary:
OpenAI has released its Frontier Governance Framework, outlining how its AI safety and security practices comply with emerging legal standards such as California's Transparency in Frontier AI Act and the EU AI Act's Code of Practice for General Purpose AI. The framework builds on OpenAI's Preparedness Framework, detailing risk assessment and mitigation strategies for advanced AI systems, including areas like cybersecurity, harmful manipulation, and loss of control.

The document also addresses model reporting, security risk management, incident response, and the incorporation of external expert input. OpenAI plans to update the framework as AI capabilities and regulatory requirements evolve, ensuring ongoing alignment with legal obligations and safety best practices.
